notice: A thinner-than-usual day for research and open source, but a massive one for silicon. AMD went full-stack at Advancing AI 2026, and the inference chip money keeps flowing.

lead.title: Helios is AMD's biggest bet yet — and OpenAI is already on stage for it
lead.summary: AMD didn't just launch a GPU at Advancing AI 2026. It launched an entire rack: 72 MI455X chips with 432GB of HBM4 each, 2nm compute chiplets, and a claimed 2.9 exaflops of FP4 inference per rack. The customer list reads like the frontier lab roster — OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle — with Sam Altman personally confirming Helios goes online in Q4 2026. The claim that matters: 30% more inference tokens per dollar than the leading competitor. If that holds in production, the Nvidia tax just got negotiable.

top_stories.title: Etched defies the skeptics: $300M Series C at a $10.3B valuation
top_stories.summary: The transformer-ASIC bet is paying off. Sequoia led the round with a16z, Jane Street and SK hynix, and Etched claims $1B in booked orders for its inference chips.

top_stories.title: xAI's Grok Build can now orchestrate 1,024 parallel agents
top_stories.summary: Workflows turns plain-language tasks into fan-out agent swarms that verify results and save themselves as reusable slash commands. The agent-orchestration race is moving from frameworks to products.

items.title: Vera Rubin NVL72 delivers 5x more tokens per dollar than GB200, says SemiAnalysis
items.summary: The deep dive numbers are in: a new 3-bit programmable LUT tensor core, $3.57 per GPU-hour TCO, and — the kicker — at 350 tokens/second/user, neither GB200 nor GB300 can serve the workload. Only Rubin can. CoreWeave's own benchmarks go further, claiming 10x throughput per megawatt. The power-constrained datacenter era has its new unit of account.

items.title: CoreWeave benchmarks Vera Rubin: 10x tokens per megawatt over Blackwell
items.summary: First independent benchmark results confirm Nvidia's efficiency claims, measured on DeepSeek R1 at matched interactivity. For datacenter operators planning next-gen builds, tokens-per-megawatt is now the metric that decides procurement.

items.title: AMD's Kria platform is an open bet on physical AI
items.summary: CPU, GPU and NPU on a single COM-HPC module with unified memory, targeted at autonomous robotics. While Nvidia sells ecosystems, AMD is selling openness — the industry's first fully integrated open platform for robotics developers.

items.title: Corgi's third round in eight weeks: AI insurance at a $4B valuation
items.summary: Three rounds in eight weeks is either a bubble signature or a signal that AI-native insurance is compounding faster than anyone modeled. $450M projected ARR suggests the latter — for now.

items.title: AegisAI raises $36M to fight AI-driven spear phishing with AI
items.summary: Founded by former Google security execs and backed by Battery, Accel and Foundation Capital. The attack surface is now LLM-generated; the defense has to be too.

items.title: Echo routes across open-weight models to hit Fable-class quality at a third of the cost
items.summary: An adaptive model built on a pool of open weights — GLM-5.2, Kimi K2.7 and others — that dynamically picks the cheapest adequate model per task. The frontier labs sell intelligence; Echo sells arbitrage on it.

items.title: Runway's Media Router picks your generative model by cost, speed or quality
items.summary: As generative media gets crowded, the value moves up the stack to routing. Runway is betting developers would rather delegate model selection than benchmark every new release themselves.

items.title: PromptQL wants shared AI threads to replace your Slack channels
items.summary: From the Hasura team: an AI-native workspace that captures tribal knowledge across databases and SaaS apps, builds task-specific agents on the fly, and compiles a self-writing wiki of how the business actually operates. Ambitious — but the knowledge-compounding angle is the right one.

items.title: OneCLI keeps your API keys out of the agent's context window
items.summary: An open-source credential gateway that intercepts secrets before they reach AI agents. Every team running coding agents against production services needs this layer; almost none have it.

items.title: OpenCode Superapp: Codex-class coding with local models and voice
items.summary: A unified coding assistant that runs online or offline, pairing agentic coding with self-hosted models. The local-first coding stack keeps maturing.

items.title: Google's quantum computer now corrects its own errors mid-computation
items.summary: The system learns from its own errors and retunes itself in real time, beating expert human calibration. Self-correcting quantum hardware removes one of the last human bottlenecks to long quantum computations.

items.title: The Kimi K-3 distillation allegations, and why investors are spooked
items.summary: Claims that Chinese labs distilled Kimi K-3 at industrial scale have triggered sanctions talk. The deeper anxiety: cheaper models undercutting OpenAI and Anthropic, circular financing, and runaway CapEx all feeding market FUD.

items.title: Apple is reportedly refreshing every Mac for the AI demand wave
items.summary: New versions across iMac, MacBook Pro and MacBook Air through fall 2026 and 2027. Apple sees local AI workloads as the upgrade driver the Mac line has been waiting for.
